newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO'S LOPEZ GETS SURPRISE CALL-UP FOR SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO'S LOPEZ GETS SURPRISE CALL-UP FOR SPAIN.

text.p: Outspoken Spanish coach Javier Clemente has once again courted controversy by naming a defender who has started just seven league matches this season in his squad for next week's vital World Cup qualifier against Yugoslavia.
Atletico Madrid's Juan Lopez is the only surprise in the 19-strong party for a match which could well decide who wins European group six.
Spain lead the group with 16 points from six matches, one ahead of Yugoslavia and four ahead of third-placed Slovakia.
There is no place in the squad for Lopez's teammate, midfielder Jose Luis Caminero, who is nursing a leg injury.
His absence means the playmaker role will once again fall to Josep Guardiola who has combined well with Real Madrid teenager Raul Gonzalez in recent games.

Raul looks set to take the left side of the attack alongside Alfonso Perez, who has led Real Betis to third in the Spanish league and is the only player challenging Brazilian Ronaldo in the Spanish goalscoring tables.

The backbone of the side is once again formed by seven Barcelona players -- Guardiola among them -- who will join Clemente's training sessions after playing the second leg of their European Cup Winners' Cup semifinal against Fiorentina on Thursday.
There are no Spanish first division matches scheduled for the weekend of April 26, giving most of the players nearly two weeks to work together.
Goalkeepers - Andoni Zubizarreta (Valencia) Santiago Canizares (Real Madrid)

Defenders - Juan Lopez (Atletico Madrid), Abelardo Fernandez, Miguel Angel Nadal, Sergi Barjuan (Barcelona), Rafael Alkorta, Fernando Hierro (Real Madrid), Agustin Aranzabal (Real Sociedad), Roberto Rios (Real Betis)
Midfielders - Julen Guerrero (Athletic Bilbao), Josep Guardiola, Luis Enrique Martinez, Guillermo Amor (Barcelona)
Forwards - Kiko Narvaez (Atletico Madrid), Juan Pizzi (Barcelona), Alfonso Perez (Real Betis), Raul Gonzalez (Real Madrid), Javier Manjarin (Deportivo Coruna)
